region.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, nominally Ottoman after the Treaty of Berlin

ledger.note: 1878 (the page gives the treaty only as 1878; the month is left out on purpose so that the land is the Ottoman Empire's before the occupation of 29 July 1878 that the austria-hungary dossier records as an occupation of Ottoman land, ledger/2). "The Treaty of Berlin caused Bosnia and Herzegovina to nominally remain under sovereignty of the Ottoman Empire"; "The occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina started on 29 July 1878"; the Bosnia Vilayet "officially remained part of the Ottoman Empire". Request R123: the dissolve no longer hands the land to Austria-Hungary as direct land; the occupation itself is not coded in this dossier because an occupation_start here would make Austria-Hungary the occupier of the eyalet's land, which the dissolve then releases as plain Austro-Hungarian land. Of the patch p1870-p1879 events/1-3 (loss to the Ottoman Empire, Ottoman gain from Austria-Hungary, occupation_start), only events/1 is now redundant: events/2-3 must stay while ottoman-empire ledger/196 (loss of Bosnia and Herzegovina to austria-hungary, July 1878) exists, because once this loss has made the land Ottoman, that event hands it to Austria-Hungary as direct land, and events/2-3 (September 1878) return it as Ottoman land under Austro-Hungarian occupation (reviewer fx-47).

region.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, nominally Ottoman until the annexation of 1908

ledger.note: 1878: the eyalet (Bosnia Vilayet) ends as a province when Austria-Hungary occupies it: "Austria-Hungary invaded and occupied Bosnia" (Bosnia Vilayet page); formal Ottoman sovereignty lasted until the annexation of 1908 (Condominium page: the Treaty of Berlin left Bosnia and Herzegovina "nominally" under Ottoman sovereignty; occupation from 29 July 1878). Request R123: the dissolve passes the land to the Ottoman Empire (it was austria-hungary); the loss before it (ledger/19) returns the land to the nominal sovereign, and the austria-hungary dossier draws the occupation.

wars.name: Great Turkish War

zones.text: the Slavonian, Lika and Dalmatian sanjaks

wars.outcome: The Ottoman defeat ended at Karlowitz in 1699; the eyalet lost the Slavonian sanjaks, the Lika sanjak and much of the Dalmatian coast.
wars.note: The page names the war and the peak of 1683; the war's years are taken from those two dates.

wars.name: Bosnian uprising of Husein Gradaščević
wars.outcome: The rebels occupied Travnik in 1831, demanding autonomy; crushed with the help of Ali-paša Rizvanbegović, who received the Herzegovina Eyalet in 1833.
wars.note: The Bosnia Eyalet page gives the Tuzla meeting of 20 January to 5 February 1831; neither page dates the rebels' defeat.

certainty.note: Sanjak frontiers against the Habsburgs and Venice moved with the campaigns of the Long Turkish and Great Turkish wars.

The Habsburg and Venetian frontier is a treaty line (Karlowitz 1699, Passarowitz 1718, Belgrade 1739); the Montenegrin and Serbian frontiers are soft, and the 1833 Herzegovina boundary is only a list of kazas.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row; six new keyframes at county level because the page gives no map (the infobox area, if any, was not shown to me; the only figure is 52,530 km2 for 1853). Disagreements: capital dates (infobox Banja Luka 1553-1639, Bosna-Saray 1639-1699, Travnik 1699-1832; body text Sarajevo 1639-1697, Travnik from 1697; the fire in 1703; return in 1850); the 1580 sanjak list differs between the footnote and Evliya Çelebi. The Sanjak of Novi Pazar and Prizren are not on the Bosnia Vilayet page, so the Ottoman-kept Novi Pazar of 1878 is not drawn. Gaps: Passarowitz terms (page silent), the 1739 treaty, Sistova 1791 (page silent), the end of the 1831 revolt, Omer Pasha 1850 (page silent). The 1878 end is the Austro-Hungarian occupation; the de jure vilayet to 1908 is not drawn. Counterparts needing dossiers: herzegovina-eyalet (written in this batch), Husein Gradaščević's Bosnian rebels (1831-1832, <10 years), Kingdom of Slavonia / Habsburg Croatia. Wikidata id null (unreachable). Rumelia Eyalet (Viçitrina and Prizren sanjaks) not written. Review fix (2026-11-01): (1) The Bosnia shape of 1580-1698 now subtracts the venetian-dalmatia keyframe of the same years and is split to follow the Venetian gains (1669, 1686, 1687, 1688, 1690, 1694), each recorded as a loss with counterpart venetian-dalmatia; the single 1699 loss of the Dalmatian coast is gone, and the 1699 gain is the Bosnian land Venice gave back at Karlowitz. The Lika and Slavonian loss of 1699 to the Military Frontier stays. (2) Herceg Novi is added to the Bosnian shape to 1686 as a town of the Sanjak of Herzegovina (the researcher's reading; the Bosnia Eyalet page does not name it) so that venetian-dalmatia's 1687 gain has a counterpart that loses it. (3) The Herzegovina kazas outside today's Bosnia and Herzegovina (Nikšić, Pljevlja, Prijepolje, Kolašin, Šaranci with Drobnjak) are added to the keyframes of 1580-1832 and 1851-1878, as the reviewer asked; the widened kaza list is the one of herzegovina-eyalet (citation needed on its page). (4) The Čitluk-Gabela strip is out of the 1699-1717 shape because Venice kept it to 1718. Disagreement with the reviewer: none beyond that. Not done: Prizren, Vicitrina and Novi Pazar remain undrawn. The Senj frontier circle of habsburg-military-frontier (14.9 E, 44.99 N, 25 km) is subtracted from Licko-Senjska in the keyframes of 1580-1698, because the Frontier drew it in the same years (3 cells shared); the Lika sanjak loss of 1699 keeps the whole county. The Bjelopavlići and Piperi land that Montenegro gained in 1796 (Danilovgrad and the 25 km circle round 19.1 E, 42.65 N) is subtracted from the Herzegovina kaza union, because the Piperi circle reached over Nikšić and Kolašin (2 cells shared with prince-bishopric-of-montenegro from 1796).
R123 (3 Nov 2026): the 1878 end no longer hands Bosnia to Austria-Hungary as direct land. Loss to ottoman-empire (1878, no month so that it comes before the occupation of 29 July) and dissolve to ottoman-empire; identity.successors austria-hungary -> ottoman-empire. The occupation is in the austria-hungary dossier (ledger/2, 4, 5). Window patch p1870-p1879 events/1 duplicates this; events/2-3 must stay while ottoman-empire ledger/196 (July 1878 loss of Bosnia and Herzegovina to austria-hungary) exists, since it hands the now-Ottoman land to Austria-Hungary as direct land (reviewer fx-47).
